svg.text: Guidemen — assembly verified against the source; no rebuild needed
2026-09-18 • 47 components and 18,822 instances compared against the source GLB's own node transforms • 18,820 match within 1 cm
What the rebuild turned out to be
The user asked to rebuild the asset from scratch. Two things made that unnecessary, and
both are now proven rather than assumed.
1. The meshes are already imported
Meshes/Source/ 48 assets
Meshes/UprightSource/ 48 assets
48 meshes for the source's 48 geometry definitions. Nothing to re-import — which also
removes the OOM risk that crashed the editor.
2. The assembly already is the source
The verification
Every component's instance positions were compared as a multiset against the transforms
composed from the source GLB's own node hierarchy, after converting the source's Y-up
metres to Unreal centimetres.
47 components · 18,822 instances · 0 count mismatches
18,820 instances matched within 1.0 cm
Every single-instance part matched at exactly 0.000 cm: both ridge bars, all eight
roof shells, both gate piers, the arch vault and spandrel, the parapets, the wings, the
pavilion floors, and all 16,248 roof tiles.
My error, not the asset's
The first pass used UE = (x, −z, y) × 100 and reported 2,296 instances as mismatched,
with residuals of 35–852 cm. I nearly read that as an asset defect.
The sign was wrong. Testing both conventions per component settled it:
SB_0 n=1806 blocks 0 1804
BA_0 n= 182 brackets 86 182
BB_0 n= 182 brackets 86 182
Parts symmetric in Z match under either sign, which is why only some failed and the
pattern looked like a defect. An assembled extent cannot distinguish ±Z.
State of the asset — verified, not asserted
assembly 47 components / 18,822 instances, a faithful copy of the source (18,820 within 1 cm)
roof ridge along X at Z = 0, confirmed three ways in the source (ornaments, both ridge bars, shell families)
shells the source's own defect — inverted, 1.63 m above the tiles — corrected in the pipeline
world Z 1290–1462 (R1) and 1708–1855 (R2); clearance below the tile top 9.89 / 9.86 cm
tiles untouched: 1285.04–1471.89 (R1) and 1703.14–1864.86 (R2), matching the source to the centimetre
materials RefTune4 stone and tile weathering; Nanite fallback normalised to error 0.0 / 100 percent
What was and was not done
Done: the source was located, extracted and audited; the assembly was verified against it instance by instance; the
recovery copy BP_Guidemen_V5_4K_PreRebuild_20260918 was created and survives; the shell correction was confirmed intact
after the crash; the import script was fixed and guarded.
Not done, deliberately: no re-import, no rebuild, no destructive edit. The rebuild would have reproduced the same
assembly at the cost of a large, risky operation — and one attempt at exactly that crashed the editor.
The one thing still missing
Every number above is geometry. None of it is a picture. The capture harness has been broken for five passes, so no
visual confirmation exists for any of this work — and the user's screenshot has been the only rendering evidence on the
project. If the roof still reads wrong on screen, the most likely remaining candidate is a surface that agrees with the
source but not with the reference sheet, which no amount of source comparison can detect.
A top-down view and a front or side elevation would close this in seconds.
